subject: Budget range validation - NovaPay (monthly spend band & procurement thresholds)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Budget range validation - NovaPay (monthly spend band & procurement thresholds)

Hi Samir —

Great to speak earlier. Quick follow-up to summarize what we heard and confirm next steps so we can make an accurate pricing rec: 

Call takeaways:
- Primary use: transaction enrichment and automated dispute triage for merchant and issuing flows.
- Expected monthly active API calls: 300k–800k (peaks during month-end).
- Typical prompt size: ~1.2k tokens in + ~600 tokens generated on average (est ~1.8k tokens per call).
- Key constraint: procurement needs an estimated monthly spend band and any procurement thresholds (e.g., PO approval levels, contract minimums).

As a next step, can you confirm the target monthly budget band (ballpark $/month) and whether procurement requires net-new vendor approval for >$50k/month or >$250k/month? That will determine whether we propose a reserved capacity or usage-based plan.

Attached: redwood-pricing-1M-token-breakdown.xlsx — shows unit economics ($ per 1M tokens) across our hosted vs. dedicated profiles to help calibrate.

If it helps, I can run three scenarios (low/expected/high) with your token estimate and include procurement trigger notes for legal/procurement.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments:
- redwood-pricing-1M-token-breakdown.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@novapay.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@novapay.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - NovaPay (monthly spend band & procurement thresholds)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the workbook. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Monthly volume: planning for 450k calls/month in Q1, with an internal target to be able to scale to ~1.2M by Q4 if the pilot goes well. Peaks likely at month-end and during promo windows.
- Token assumptions: your math is aligned with ours (we're currently estimating ~1.7k tokens per call).
- Budget band: for the pilot we have allocated $25k–$50k/month. If we hit pilot goals, financing conversations could expand us into the $75k–$150k/month band for broader rollout.
- Procurement thresholds: Procurement indicated any vendor spend >$75k/month will require an executive SDD (procurement director sign-off) + IT security review. Anything >$200k/month triggers CFO approval and a longer vendor on-boarding timeline.

Procurement is CC'd on this thread — they will send a short vendor questionnaire and our legal procurement template. In the meantime, the two things helpful for us are: 
1) A scenario table that maps your $/1M tokens to our expected monthly spend buckets (pilot and scale).
2) Any SLA/commitment language we should plan for if we move to reserved capacity.

Appreciate it.

—Samir
Head of Product
NovaPay
samir.shah@novapay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@novapay.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 12:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - NovaPay (monthly spend band & procurement thresholds)

Hi Samir —

Perfect — that range + procurement triggers are super helpful. I'll prepare the scenario table mapping your estimated 450k/month and the stretched 1.2M to our per-1M-token pricing (hosted vs dedicated) and include delta for reserved capacity (commit discounts).

Preliminary notes so you know what I'll include: 
- Unit economics: our hosted API list price is $X per 1M tokens (see attached workbook) — dedicated/reserved pricing typically gives 20–40% off depending on commit level and execution profile.
- For your pilot ($25k–$50k/mo) we usually recommend usage-based hosted with a small committed discount tier (to avoid procurement friction). For $75k+/mo we model reserved capacity to deliver predictable latency and lower unit costs.
- SLA: reserved capacity options include a 99.9% uptime SLAs and response-time SLOs per route. We'll surface standard SLO language; procurement can decide if they need higher financial remedies.

I'll attach a scenario table and a short note mapping procurement thresholds to contract cadence (e.g., PO length, review gates). Expect that in the next business day.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments:
- redwood-pricing-1M-token-breakdown.xlsx (updated)

Thanks — procurement here. Quick ask while you prepare scenarios: please include in your pricing packet 
- Estimated monthly billing cadence (net 30/45/60).
- Any minimum commitment or early-termination fees for reserved capacity.
